about: LanEx's glossary: one entry per term, the short line is what hovering a label shows (term.js), the whole entry is Help, Learn. ids are lower-kebab; aliases are other spellings people search for.

rtl.short: Hardware described as registers and the logic between them, in Verilog, SystemVerilog or VHDL. The input to the flow.
rtl.lanex: The ticked design files under Sources are the RTL a run builds.

top-module.short: The module that is the chip: every other module sits inside it. Its ports become the chip's pins.
top-module.lanex: DESIGN_NAME in the config. The die, the pins and the reports take its name.

hierarchy.short: Modules inside modules. LibreLane flattens them into one netlist by default, so instance names become paths like u_core.u_alu.

synthesis.short: Turns the RTL into a netlist of the PDK's standard cells. LibreLane uses Yosys for it.
synthesis.lanex: Run up to Synthesis (Run menu) gives the cell count and area in seconds.

synth-strategy.short: How synthesis maps the logic (SYNTH_STRATEGY): AREA 0 to 3 favour fewer, smaller cells; DELAY 0 to 4 build faster logic at more area. Only trying shows which is best for a design.

slang.short: USE_SLANG reads the design with the Slang frontend instead of Yosys's built-in reader, for SystemVerilog the built-in one refuses: import, interfaces, structs.

define.short: `define values the flow passes to every Verilog file (VERILOG_DEFINES), as NAME or NAME=value, so the same RTL can build different ways.

netlist.short: The design as cell instances and the wires (nets) between them. Synthesis writes it; every later step works on it.

standard-cell.short: A pre-drawn, pre-characterised gate or flip-flop of a fixed height that sits in a row. Names read library__function_drive, such as sky130_fd_sc_hd__nand2_1.

drive-strength.short: The _1, _2, _4 at the end of a cell name: a bigger number drives more load, faster, and costs area and power.

scl.short: One family of cells for a PDK, such as sky130_fd_sc_hd (high density). Libraries trade speed, area and leakage.

liberty.short: The tables of delay, power and area of every cell, at one corner. Synthesis and timing analysis read them.

pdk.short: The foundry's layers, design rules, device models and cell libraries for one manufacturing process.
pdk.lanex: sky130A, gf180mcuD and ihp-sg13g2 are the open ones LanEx installs.

clock-period.short: The time between two rising clock edges, in ns. Every register-to-register path has to fit in it. MHz = 1000 / period.
clock-period.lanex: 10 ns is 100 MHz. A smaller period is a faster chip and harder to meet.

clock-port.short: The top module's input that carries the clock (CLOCK_PORT). Timing is checked against it.
clock-port.lanex: Wrong or empty, and no register-to-register path is timed: the run can look clean with nothing checked.

slack.short: Time left over on a path: when the data has to arrive minus when it does. Positive meets timing; negative misses by that much.

setup.short: The check that data arrives early enough before the next clock edge. It fails when the logic is too slow for the clock.
setup.lanex: A slower clock (a bigger period) fixes it; so can less logic between registers.

hold.short: The check that data doesn't change too soon after a clock edge. A slower clock doesn't help; the flow adds delay buffers.
hold.lanex: The hold margins tell the repair steps how far past zero to aim.

wns.short: The slack of the single worst path. LibreLane reports the worst slack, which is positive when every path passes.

tns.short: The sum of the slack of every failing endpoint. It tells one bad path apart from five hundred slightly late ones.

endpoint.short: Where a timing path ends: a flip-flop's data pin or an output port. "12 failing endpoints" means data is late at 12 places.

timing-path.short: From a start (an input or a flip-flop) through logic to an end (a flip-flop or an output): register to register, input to register, register to output, or input to output.

sta.short: Checks every path from the cells' delays and the wires' estimated delays, without simulating. LibreLane runs it after synthesis, during place and route, and at sign-off.

corner.short: One set of process, voltage and temperature: tt is typical, ss slow, ff fast. LibreLane's names add the wire corner, as in max_ss_100C_1v60.
corner.lanex: On sky130 a run fails only on the tt corners (TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS); the others warn.

io-delay.short: The share of the clock period LibreLane's own constraints give the world outside the chip on every input and output (IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT, 20 % each).

sdc.short: Timing constraints written in Tcl: clocks, input and output delays, loads. LibreLane writes one from CLOCK_PORT and CLOCK_PERIOD unless PNR_SDC_FILE and SIGNOFF_SDC_FILE name your own.

floorplan.short: The first physical step: the die and core size, the rows, the pins and where macros go.

die.short: The whole rectangle of the chip or block, edge to edge (DIE_AREA, x0 y0 x1 y1 in µm).
die.lanex: Utilization sizing works it out from the cells; a fixed die area sets it.

core.short: The area inside the die where cells go, in rows: the die minus the margins. Pins sit outside it, on the die's edge.

core-margin.short: The gap between the die's edge and the core, left for pins and power: on sky130 hd, 4 rows top and bottom (10.88 µm) and 12 sites left and right (5.52 µm).

utilization.short: How much of the core the cells fill, in %. When LibreLane sizes the die, it makes the core the cells' area divided by FP_CORE_UTIL.
utilization.lanex: 50 % gives a core twice the cells' area; the rest is room for buffers, the clock tree and wires.

placement-density.short: How tightly global placement packs cells locally (PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT). Lower spreads them out for routing; higher clusters them.
placement-density.lanex: By default utilization + 10. It doesn't help when placement says the core is full: that needs a bigger core.

aspect-ratio.short: The core's height divided by its width (FP_ASPECT_RATIO); 1 is square.

row-site.short: Cells sit in rows; a row is a line of sites, the smallest step a cell can move (sky130 hd: 0.46 × 2.72 µm).

tap-cell.short: A small cell placed every few µm in each row that ties the wells to power and ground, so the chip can't latch up.

endcap.short: The cells at both ends of each row that close off the wells.

tie-cell.short: A cell whose output is a constant 0 or 1, used instead of wiring a gate's input straight to power or ground.

fill-decap.short: Cells added after routing to fill the empty space in the rows. Fill keeps the layers even for manufacturing; decap also steadies the supply.

macro.short: A pre-built block placed whole: an SRAM, an analog block, or a design hardened in another run. LibreLane doesn't place macros by itself.
macro.lanex: Cells & macros, Macros adds and arranges them.

halo.short: Keep-out space around a macro where no cell may go, left for wires and power straps.

pin.short: Where a top-level port meets the die's edge, on a metal layer. Each one needs its own place on a routing track.
pin.lanex: IO_PIN_ORDER_CFG picks the side and order of each pin.

pdn.short: The metal network that brings power and ground to every cell: rails along the rows, straps across them, sometimes rings around the core.

strap.short: One wide power or ground wire of the grid, repeated at a fixed pitch and offset (PDN_VPITCH, PDN_VOFFSET).

ir-drop.short: Voltage lost along the power grid's resistance, so the cells far from the supply see a little less than the supply voltage.

placement.short: Gives every cell its position in the rows: global placement spreads them to keep wires short, detailed placement makes every position legal.

global-placement.short: Spreads the cells over the core to shorten the wires, with overlaps still allowed (OpenROAD's RePlAce).

detailed-placement.short: Moves every cell to a legal, non-overlapping spot in a row.
detailed-placement.lanex: It fails with DPL-0036 when an area is too full.

cts.short: Builds a tree of buffers so the clock reaches every flip-flop at nearly the same time.

clock-skew.short: The difference in clock arrival between two flip-flops. It eats setup or hold time on the paths between them.

buffer.short: A cell that repeats its input, to drive more load or a longer wire, or to add delay.

resizer.short: OpenROAD steps that change cell sizes and insert buffers to fix slew, capacitance, fanout and timing.

slew.short: How long a signal takes to switch. Slow edges cost delay and power; the PDK sets a limit (MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT, 0.75 ns on sky130A).
slew.lanex: LibreLane warns about it and finishes the run.

max-cap.short: The most load a driver may see, its loads' input pins plus the wire. Above it the driver is slow and its delay is extrapolated.

fanout.short: How many inputs one output drives. Above MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT (10) design repair splits the net with buffers.

routing.short: Draws the wires that connect every pin: global routing plans them, detailed routing draws them.

global-routing.short: Plans which regions and layers each net uses, on a coarse grid, before any wire is drawn. It reports congestion.

detailed-routing.short: Draws the real wires and vias on the tracks, under the spacing rules (OpenROAD's TritonRoute). What it can't fix is a routing DRC error.

congestion.short: More wires want to pass through an area than it has tracks for; overflow counts the excess.
congestion.lanex: The fix is room (a lower utilization or density) or more layers.

metal-layer.short: One wiring level of the stack (sky130: li1, met1 to met5). Low layers are thin and dense; high ones carry power and long wires.
metal-layer.lanex: Top routing layer (RT_MAX_LAYER) keeps signals below a layer.

via.short: A connection between two neighbouring metal layers.

track.short: A line on a metal layer where a wire may run, at that layer's pitch (sky130 met2: 0.46 µm).

wirelength.short: The total length of every routed wire. Longer means more delay, more power and more congestion.

antenna.short: During manufacturing a long wire collects charge before it is connected to anything that can drain it, and can damage the transistor gate it ends on.
antenna.lanex: Fixed with a protection diode, or a jump to a higher layer near the gate.

diode.short: A small cell that drains that charge safely. LibreLane inserts them during antenna repair; DIODE_ON_PORTS adds one on every input or output pin.

parasitics.short: The resistance and capacitance of the real wires, extracted from the layout into a SPEF file. Sign-off timing uses them.

drc.short: Every shape against the foundry's rules for width, spacing and enclosure.
drc.lanex: Magic and KLayout run the PDK's rule decks on the GDS; the router checks only its own wires.

lvs.short: The circuit rebuilt from the drawn layout, compared with the netlist (Netgen). A mismatch means the chip that would be made isn't your circuit.

xor.short: LibreLane writes the final GDS twice, with Magic and with KLayout, and compares them shape by shape. Any difference is flagged.

gds.short: The final layout: every polygon on every layer. What a foundry or a shuttle receives.

lef-def.short: LEF describes cells and macros (size, pins, blockages); DEF describes one design's placement and wires.
lef-def.lanex: Every stage before the final GDS is shown from its DEF.

lint.short: Checking the RTL for mistakes without building it (Verilator): undeclared wires, width mismatches, latches.
lint.lanex: Check syntax in the RTL IDE runs the same check the flow's first step does.

latch.short: A storage element that is transparent while its enable is on. Usually inferred by mistake: an always @(*) that doesn't give a signal a value on every path.
latch.lanex: LibreLane's linter stops the run on one.

eqy.short: A formal proof that the netlist does what the RTL does (Yosys EQY). Off by default in LibreLane.

disconnected-pin.short: A cell pin no wire reaches after routing.

illegal-overlap.short: Two cells, or a cell and a macro, overlapping where that isn't allowed, found while extracting the layout.

signoff.short: The final checks before a chip is made: timing with the real wires in every corner, DRC, LVS and antenna.
signoff.lanex: LanEx shows LibreLane's checks. A foundry's own sign-off uses its own rule decks: LanEx is not a sign-off tool.

power.short: Switching power (charging wires), internal power (inside cells) and leakage (always on). LibreLane assumes a default switching activity, so it is an estimate.

testbench.short: Simulation-only Verilog that drives the design, compares what comes out with what should, and ends with PASS, or with FAIL and an error exit.
testbench.lanex: Every LanEx example ships one; Simulate in the RTL IDE runs it.

run-step-stage.short: A run is one pass of the flow; a step is one LibreLane step (OpenROAD.GlobalPlacement); a stage groups steps (Synthesis, Floorplan … Sign-off).
